messages:
samir: FYI escalated from acct ACCT-984, they're seeing p99 blow up on streaming endpoints only. Non-streaming (sync) calls look fine. Symptoms: first byte arrives quickly, but stream stalls between chunks -> user sees long total time and UI hangs. Sending full headers/logs below.

maria_g: Oof, how many users affected? region? any recent deploys to streaming runtime?

samir: Single customer reported but spike visible in metrics for a few hosts in us-west1 between 10:12-10:28 UTC. No obvious deploys in that window per deploy-bot. Repro steps included native SSE client + curl. I attached a minimal repro curl below.

samir: Repro (curl):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-xyz" -v
```
Behavior: curl prints first event quickly, then nothing for ~12s, then several events burst. Chrome fetch() shows similar: first chunk -> long pause -> remainder.

ingrid: Do we have chunk timings by host? Could be edge/proxy coalescing or gzip buffer at load balancer. Alex, can you pull p50/p95 inter-chunk intervals from the runtime traces for that window?

alex_k: Looking now. Traces show server emitted chunks every ~300ms, but tcp packet capture from our LB shows bursts at ~12s. So server seems fine, something in front is coalescing. We have a couple of CloudEdge (third-party CDN) nodes with increased buffer size at that time.

dylan_s: Common culprits: intermediate proxy enabling gzip/deflate which buffers until enough bytes; missing SSE event newline; Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding mismatches; or HTTP/2 flow control differences. Also Chrome on mobile can buffer small chunks until a certain size.

samir: Customer uses their own prod client behind an internal corporate proxy (they said). Could be their corporate proxy coalescing.

maria_g: They said only started last week. We pushed a runtime quantization change last Friday — could that have altered chunk sizes? But Alex's trace showing server chunk cadence unchanged.

ingrid: Two immediate mitigation options:
- suggest customer disable intermediates (corporate proxy bypass) to test
- temporarily route that tenant to non-streaming path (server buffers full response and sends once) as a stopgap

alex_k: Also we can try server-side quick mitigations: add explicit SSE flushes and pad chunks so proxies don't treat them as small. For nginx/front proxies use `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and `Cache-Control: no-transform`.

dylan_s: For node/express, call `res.flush()` after each write and set headers:
```
res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache, no-transform');
res.setHeader('X-Accel-Buffering','no');
res.write(':ok\n\n'); // heartbeat to force flush
```
That often defeats proxy coalescing.

alex_k: Note: some CDNs will still coalesce if gzip is on. For streaming we should recommend disabling compression for that route. We can push a temporary rule in the edge to disable gzip for `Accept: text/event-stream`.

sre-bot: [alert] edge-node cloudedge-7 reported buffer-size change, 10:11:47 UTC -> increased from 8KB to 64KB due to config drift.

samir: That aligns. Customer likely hit that node. If we flip `no-transform` and disable gzip at edge, should see immediate improvement.

maria_g: Customer asked for step-by-step repro they can run locally to rule out their proxy. Can we give them a simple python SSE client and a small server? I'll paste a minimal client + server.

dylan_s: Server (python aiohttp):
```
from aiohttp import web
async def handler(request):
    async def stream(resp):
        for i in range(10):
            await resp.write(f"data: chunk {i}\n\n".encode())
            await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    return web.Response(body=stream, headers={
        'Content-Type':'text/event-stream',
        'Cache-Control':'no-cache, no-transform',
        'X-Accel-Buffering':'no'
    })
```
Client (curl or python requests) should show steady chunks.

ingrid: Action items:
- Alex: push edge rule to disable gzip for SSE and add `no-transform` passthrough for `Accept: text/event-stream` (canary to 10% of traffic) — ETA 2h
- Samir: share repro and ask customer to test bypassing corp proxy or run local server -> confirm
- Dylan: add server-side small heartbeat + explicit flush to runtime in next minor release; include feature flag to opt out — ETA 1d
- Maria: offer tenant temporary non-streaming fallback (support toggle) and update ticket with mitigation steps — ETA 30m

samir: Customer tried bypassing corp proxy and the stream becomes normal. They confirmed improvement when curl run from a machine that goes directly to cloud (no corp proxy). So root cause confirmed: intermediate proxy coalescing.

maria_g: I've applied the non-streaming fallback for that tenant and they reported UI usable again. Keeping monitoring on p99.

alex_k: Canary edge rule deployed to 10% -> early metrics show inter-chunk intervals drop from median 12000ms -> 400ms on canary hosts. Rolling to 100% now.

sre-bot: [change] gzip disabled for SSE routes on edges (rollout 100%) at 10:48 UTC.

dylan_s: Reminder for runtime change: add padding option `stream.padding_bytes` to ensure minimum chunk size for flaky proxies. We'll track perf impact.

samir: Ticket updated and customer notified. Closing once we see stable 24h window.

support-bot: [ticket] ACCT-984 updated with mitigation steps and repro links.

maria_g: Thanks everyone. Lessons: always include edge config checks in streaming p99 investigations and provide quick non-streaming fallback for sensitive tenants.

alex_k: Also add automated synthetic tests from behind common corp-proxy emulators (small chunk sizes + gzip) to catch regressions.

samir: Agreed — will add to postmortem template. If anyone wants to add notes, please do before EOD.
